Begin Math with short percent retrieval before advancing to variables and expressions; use oral/whiteboard French automaticity; apply lens/refraction ideas to cameras; protect an early laptop-only Builder Lab; advance Ancient Greece to the Sicilian Expedition; finish and revise incomplete analytical writing; launch a 60-point-per-semester AR-weighted independent reading plan.

lessons.subject: french
lessons.previous_learning: Day 15 confirmed the negative-possession rule is still not automatic even though question wording is understood. Repeating a long written worksheet is no longer the best teaching method.
lessons.course_context: Switch to rapid oral and visual pattern training: PAS -> DE/D'.
learning_objectives: Say negative possession sentences using de/d' automatically.
Use n' before a vowel-starting form of avoir.
Reach 5/5 orally before completing a four-item written check.
lessons.why_it_matters: Automatic high-frequency patterns make speaking and writing more fluent.

vocabulary.definition: saying that someone does not have something
dropping a vowel before another vowel sound, as in ne -> n'

lessons.written_instruction: Atticus: you do not need another long worksheet. Today you will SAY the pattern until it becomes automatic. In most negative possession sentences, un/une/des becomes de, or d' before a vowel sound.

worked_examples.title: Vowel sound
worked_examples.explanation: Use d' before a vowel sound.

guided_practice.prompt: Oral only: J'ai une sœur; Nous avons des livres; Il a un ordinateur; Vous avez une voiture; Elles ont des devoirs. Say each as a negative possession sentence.

independent_practice.prompt: Make negative: Tu as un stylo.
Make negative: Elle a des questions.
Make negative: Nous avons une voiture.
Make negative: Il a un ordinateur.

exit_ticket.prompt: Oral gate: 5/5 new negative-possession sentences correct without a written model.
exit_ticket.answer: Five correct sentences using ne/n' + avoir + pas + de/d'.

lessons.voice_prompt: Speak directly to Atticus. Keep the session fast and oral. Use whiteboard_draw to write a positive possession sentence, circle un/une/des, cross it out, and replace it with DE or D'. Ask him to say the full negative sentence aloud. If he misses it, correct only the pattern, then give a NEW example. Do not make him copy explanations. Get 5/5 new oral examples before the four-item written check.
lessons.teacher_notes: Teaching method changed from repetition worksheet to oral/visual automaticity.
